prediction_text: Direction: Barack Obama is re-elected in 2012 (positive for the incumbent). Mitt Romney does not win the presidency. The Mercury retrograde beginning on election day, 6 November 2012, is read as procedural turbulence around the vote — delays, recount-type disputes or a result not cleanly settled on the night — but not as a reversal of the outcome: the incumbent retains the White House, with the result confirmed in the days following 6 November 2012 (day-scale coordinate: election day, confirmation window the following days). Confidence: moderate.
basis:
Card carries no tradition/system field; the card's question is an election-winner question whose only stated astrological datum is Mercury retrograde beginning on election day, so the system is self-decided from the card's genre as Western astrology (mundane/electional reading).
systems_used: Western astrology (mundane configuration reading; no candidate charts supplied on the card)
Reasoning: Mercury retrograde at a vote speaks to the counting/communication process, not by itself to the winner; with no charts on the card, the winner call rests on the incumbency fact stated on the card combined with the absence of any change-configuration of the 2008 type — the retrograde is therefore assigned to the process face (delays, disputed counts) and explicitly not flipped into a challenger-win call, which would be a direction change without a qualitative trigger. Object check: outcome bearer = the presidency; process turbulence and winner are kept as separate faces and not merged. Initial-direction anchor (calibration §9): initial direction = Obama re-elected, basis = incumbency plus retrograde confined to process; direction unchanged, R81-REV1 change gate not applicable. Timing: the question's own scale is the single election day, so a day-scale coordinate is proper here and is stated as election day plus a short confirmation window.
